title.narrative: Geothermal Power Generation Project

description.narrative: The project will support expansion of Indonesia's geothermal generating capacity to contribute to the sustainability and sufficiency of the electricity system, aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 7: access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all. The project will support GDE, a state-owned geothermal company focused on exploration and development of geothermal resources, to commission an additional 100 megawatts (MW) of geothermal electricity generating capacity 55 MW at the Dieng geothermal field in Central Java and 55 MW at the Patuha geothermal field in West Java.

Progress Toward Outcome: The three DMF targets for this output are ongoing. GDE has updated its communications standard operating procedures and has closely coordinated outreach and consultations with affected communities. GDE is implementing the gender-responsive community development strategy it has developed and has allocated budget 30% in 2023 for womens livelihoods and womens scholarships. Status of Implementation Progress: GDE's corporate and community communication strategy was developed in 2022, and gender-responsive communication materials both in Bahasa and English were published and are regularly being developed to align with the ongoing field activities. GDE has updated its communications standard operating procedures and has closely coordinated outreach and consultations with affected communities. These activities will continue throughout the project implementation phase.
The draft feasibility study for a geothermal direct-use project, with the potential to enhance livelihood opportunities for community members, has been revised to incorporate feedback from ADB during the loan review mission in October 2023. The PMC has submitted the final feasibility study to GDE.
GDE is implementing the gender-responsive community development strategy it has developed in 2021, with 33% budgetary allocation in 2024 for women's livelihoods and women's scholarships for Dieng and 41% for Patuha. The implementation of gender-responsive community development strategy will continue throughout the project implementation phase.
The total number of GDE staff training days dedicated to increasing knowledge in project and contract management already reached 588 days, of which, 360 (61%) training days were for male staff and 228 (39%) training days were for women staff. The target of 30% women training days have been achieved. The training will continue throughout the project implementation phase.
The Environmental Management System, which includes new facilities and integrates aspects of gender, climate, and community safety, was finalized and certified in early Q2 2023. Certifications and accreditations for ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 37001:2016 for Dieng 2 and Patuha 2 were achieved in 2022 and being renewed every three years, and SMK3 PP 50/2012 accreditation is underway.
GDE reported that 873 male staff and 146 female staff (14%) were trained in geothermal operations. The target of 10 GDE staff with at least 20% women participation was partially achieved. The training of GDE staff on geothermal operations will continue throughout the project implementation phase.
All ten wells were successfully drilled, and demobilization was completed on 14 September 2023. The civil works for roads and well pad preparations were completed while well testing activities are currently in progress. The EPC bidding documents are expected to be issued within Q2 2024, with an expected award date in Q1 2025. The commercial operations date (COD) is anticipated in Q1 2027.
All twelve wells were successfully drilled, and demobilization is expected to be completed by April 2024. The civil works for roads and well pad preparations were completed while well testing activities are currently in progress. The EPC bidding documents were finalized and issued on 2 January 2024, with an expected award date in Q4 2024. The COD for Patuha Unit 2 is anticipated in Q4 2026.
